CANONICAL GRAMMAR

Bullet-pattern glossary

The vocabulary stays stable while the geometry changes.

FAN
Several angles radiate from one source.
SWEEP
The firing direction changes over committed beats.
GAP
A dense field leaves a readable opening.
AIMED
A shot commits to the player position during the warning.
BURST
Several rapid volleys separated by recovery.
WALL
A broad obstruction pressures route choice.
SPIRAL
A rotating emission develops over time.
CROSSFIRE
Multiple origins constrain different routes.
RETURN
A familiar attack deliberately exploits a surface join.
CONVERGENCE
Independent trajectories meet later.

MANIFOLD VISUAL LANGUAGE

Real threats and chart previews

● Solid shot and continuous trail = real projectile; normal collisions apply.

◯ Hollow circle and dashed lead-in = a future-position image, not an extra shot or extra hitbox. It does NOT guarantee the identified physical shot is harmless.

Pulsing paired-edge mark = projected crossing within a fraction of a second; its arrival can still change with folds or later motion.

K / single slanted notch = Klein twist; P / opposite ticks = projective join; K+P = mixed prototype.

The Klein bottle and mathematical Dyck surface are connected, nonorientable surfaces. The current K+P boss is a Dyck-inspired gameplay chart, not yet a mathematically verified K#RP² model. There is no global "other side" whose projectiles are automatically harmless. The displays distinguish live objects from additional render-only images, not alternate collision rules.
